hyps.why: With edge 3 absent, edge 4 is the only remaining route to the output, so removing it nearly disconnects the cell.
With edge 4 absent, edge 3 is the sole direct input-to-output path, so removing it is catastrophic.
When edge 3 is the only path to the output, downgrading it from a conv to a skip removes the cell's learnable capacity.
A skip-heavy cell lacks learnable transforms, so adding a 3x3 conv on the input edge gives a much larger gain.
Replacing a parameter-free skip with a 3x3 conv adds learnable capacity, a bigger gain than filling a none or avg_pool edge.
Swapping a non-learnable pooling edge for a 3x3 conv gives a large gain, unlike edits on edges that already hold convs.
Replacing pooling with a learnable conv in a skip-dominated cell yields a big boost, while edits on skip or none edges barely change anything.
With the direct input-to-output edge missing, a skip on edge 1 adds a useful gradient and information path, whereas it is redundant or harmful when edge 3 exists.
When edge 4 is absent all signal flows through edge 3, so strengthening it helps more.
Without edge 1 the cell has fewer alternative paths, so removing the direct edge 3 cuts input from the output.
